REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 13, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
OCTOBER 13, 2022, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jeff Ludington, Generations Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Girl Scout Troop 313.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Hindu Heritage Month (Month of October).

  Friends of the Cerritos Library (National Friends of Libraries Week).

  Cerritos United Blue Girls 2005 Soccer Team (2022 Cal South National Cup Champions).

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  Councilmember Johnson requested the City Council affirm her request to remove one of her
  Let Freedom Ring Committee appointees. She presented documents to the City Council for
  the record. (Documents distributed to the City Council are considered public record. Full-
  text copies of submitted documents can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai spoke in support of the removal of the subject committee member.

  Kirit Chauhan spoke in support of the removal of the subject committee member.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to affirm Councilmember
  Johnson’s request to remove Daisy “Mina” Lagasca from the Let Freedom Ring Committee

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  An informational update was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted

  Matthew Ellis submitted written correspondence expressing concerns related to the
  wattage of the new LED street lights currently being installed at signaled intersections in

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Kirit Chauhan expressed thanks to school administrators for the work they do and
  concern regarding a local news story.

  Case van der Linden congratulated the local Hindu population for the celebration of
  Hindu Heritage Month, expressed concern regarding the City Council vote to remove a
  Let Freedom Ring Committee member, and inquired of City plans for water conservation
  and underground water management.

  Sam Desai wished the community a happy Diwali, spoke regarding his candidacy for the
  ABC Unified School District Board of Education, Trustee Area 3, expressed concerns with
  a local news story, and requested Councilmembers to provide a response to the story.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

REQUEST FOR REORDERING OF THE AGENDA

Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, requested a verbal City Council vote, pursuant to the provisions of
Section 8.09 of the City Council Protocol Manual, to reorder the agenda in order to consider
Closed Session Item 12A (described below) at this juncture of the meeting. He noted the City
Attorney’s Office received information related to the one (1) potential case under consideration
in Item 12A which may be relevant to another item on the Open Session portion of the agenda.
He affirmed the City Council should review the relevant information in Closed Session prior to
consideration of the related Open Session agenda item.

MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to consider Closed Session
Agenda Item 12A at this juncture of the meeting (COUNCIL)

The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at this juncture of the meeting, pursuant to the
aforementioned City Council action, to consider the following item as listed on the Closed
Session agenda:

12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION

CLOSED SESSION REPORT (ITEM 12A):

The City Council reconvened into Open Session. Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City
Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Item 12A, as listed on the Closed Session
agenda.

ITEM 12A MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Accept the settlement offer submitted to the Office of the City Attorney by Extra
  Space Storage, current owner of real property located at 10753 Artesia Boulevard.
  The settlement offer was made in response to a Notice of Default and Notice of
  Violation of the Cerritos Municipal Code Violation for failure to comply with recorded
  covenants and the City’s Art in Public Places Program at the property, by failing to
  maintain and prevent from being removed a City Council-approved art piece called
  “Strength of the Maker.” The substance of the settlement is summarized as follows:

  a. Extra Space Storage shall pay City the amount of $55,000.00
  b. The amount will serve as replacement for stolen art piece and Extra Space
  Storage is not required to replace any art piece on-site
  c. The amount shall be deposited into the City’s Art in Public Places Trust Fund
  d. The amount is deemed full settlement of the dispute
